documentation_xml: /// Interface to manage the Rhino main window visibility, focus, and activation monitoring. /// /// /// /// This interface provides methods to control the visibility and focus state of the Rhino /// main window when running Rhino inside another host application (e.g., AutoCAD). /// /// /// Window Activation Monitoring: /// /// /// The interface supports window activation monitoring via a Windows CBT /// (Computer Based Training) hook. A CBT hook is a low-level Windows mechanism that /// receives notifications about system events before they occur. The HCBT_ACTIVATE /// notification (hook code 5) is sent by Windows when any window is about to be activated /// (receive keyboard focus). /// /// /// This pattern is similar to Rhino.Inside.Revit's ComputerBasedTrainingHook implementation, /// which intercepts window activation to conditionally show or hide the Rhino window based on /// whether Rhino is waiting for user input (e.g., during a RhinoGet operation). /// /// /// When the Rhino window is about to be activated and Rhino is in a RhinoGet operation, /// the window is automatically shown. This enables "headless" operation where the window /// remains hidden until user interaction is actually required. /// /// /// Thread Requirements: /// /// /// CBT hooks must be installed on a thread that has a Windows message pump. The hook callback executes /// on the same thread that installed the hook. /// /// /// Lifecycle: /// /// /// Implementations must properly clean up the CBT hook when disposed. Failing to uninstall /// the hook before the application exits can cause crashes or undefined behavior. documentation_xml: /// Installs a Windows CBT (Computer Based Training) hook to monitor window activation events. /// /// /// /// What is a CBT Hook? /// /// /// A CBT hook is a Windows mechanism originally designed for Computer Based Training /// applications. It receives notifications about window management events before /// they occur, including: /// /// /// HCBT_ACTIVATE (5): A window is about to be activated /// HCBT_CREATEWND (3): A window is about to be created /// HCBT_DESTROYWND (4): A window is about to be destroyed /// HCBT_MINMAX (1): A window is about to be minimized/maximized /// /// /// This implementation specifically listens for HCBT_ACTIVATE events targeting /// the Rhino main window. /// /// /// Why Use This Pattern? /// /// /// When running Rhino in "headless" mode inside AutoCAD, the Rhino window is initially /// hidden. However, certain operations (like RhinoGet point picking) require /// user interaction with the Rhino window. The CBT hook detects when the Rhino window /// is attempting to activate and automatically shows the window if Rhino is waiting /// for user input (i.e., RhinoGet.InGet() returns true). /// /// /// This is the same pattern used by Rhino.Inside.Revit's ComputerBasedTrainingHook. /// /// /// Thread Requirements: /// /// /// The hook must be installed on a thread with a Windows message pump. This is a /// thread-local hook (installed with dwThreadId = GetCurrentThreadId()), meaning /// it only receives events for windows owned by the current thread. When running inside /// AutoCAD, install from the main UI thread. /// /// /// Lifecycle: /// /// /// The hook remains active until is called or the /// object is disposed. The hook is automatically uninstalled when /// is called. /// /// /// Idempotency: /// /// /// Calling this method multiple times is safe. If a hook is already installed, subsequent /// calls do nothing. Similarly, if no window has been set via , /// the method returns without installing a hook (there's nothing to monitor). /// /// /// Delegate Lifetime: /// /// /// The hook callback delegate must remain alive for the entire duration the hook is /// installed. The implementation stores the delegate as a field to prevent garbage /// collection. If the delegate were collected while the hook is active, Windows would /// call invalid memory, causing an application crash. /// /// /// /// /// // Set up the window manager /// windowManager.SetWindow(RhinoApp.MainWindowHandle()); /// /// // Start monitoring - window will auto-show when RhinoGet.InGet() is true /// windowManager.InstallActivationHook(); /// /// ///

documentation_xml: /// Base class for Grasshopper components that create Civil 3D objects. /// Provides optional "Replace" functionality that tracks all created objects /// and automatically deletes them before creating new ones when the solver re-runs. /// Supports multi-input components where SolveInstance is called N times for N inputs. /// /// /// Rhino Undo/Redo Protection /// /// This class implements protection against a crash that occurs when Civil 3D objects /// are created immediately after a Rhino undo/redo operation. The issue manifests as an /// inside AeccDbMgd.dll (Civil 3D's /// managed database layer) when calling Alignment.Create() or similar Civil 3D /// object creation methods. /// /// Root Cause /// /// When the user performs an undo in Rhino (e.g., undoing a curve move), the Grasshopper /// solver is triggered to re-run. The solver receives the IsEndUndo event and runs /// immediately after, but Civil 3D's internal state is still unstable at this point. /// Even though our transaction state appears clean (0 active transactions, successful /// document lock), Civil 3D's native layer crashes when attempting to create new objects. /// /// Solution /// /// The fix is to defer object creation by one solve cycle after undo/redo completes: /// /// IsBeginUndo fires → Set _undoInProgress = true /// IsEndUndo fires → Set _justFinishedUndo = true /// BeforeSolveInstance runs → Detect _justFinishedUndo, skip this solve, schedule re-solve in 100ms /// Re-solve runs → Civil 3D is now stable, object creation succeeds /// /// /// /// Tracked objects are preserved during skip because Civil 3D objects are not affected by /// Rhino undo - they remain valid and should be deleted when the deferred solve runs (if /// Replace mode is enabled). /// /// /// Derived classes must call at the start of their /// SolveInstance method and return early if it returns true. /// ///

/// A Grasshopper component that creates an AutoCAD Block Table Record (a block definition)
/// from Rhino and AutoCAD geometry. The definition is written straight into the document's
/// Block Table and can be fed to the Create AutoCAD Block Reference component to place
/// instances of it.

/// geometry and native AutoCAD entities can be mixed freely on the one input. The component
/// owns exactly one block definition: while its inputs change it redefines that same record

/// and pick up the new geometry rather than being orphaned.

    ///     shape using the minor-to-major radius ratio

    /// </remarks>

<summary>
    /// Produces a valid knot vector for Rhino's NURBS representation from a source knot vector.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="inputKnots">
    /// A non-empty, non-decreasing sequence of knot values from the source system.
    /// </param>
    /// <param name="degree">
    /// The polynomial degree of the NURBS curve.
    /// </param>
    /// <param name="numberOfControlPoints">
    /// The number of control points on the curve.
    /// </param>
    /// <returns>
    /// A knot vector containing exactly <c>degree + numberOfControlPoints - 1</c> values.
    /// </returns>
    /// <remarks>
    /// AutoCAD uses a D + N + 1 knot convention while Rhino uses D + N - 1.
    /// This method normalizes the knot vector by:
    /// <list type="bullet">

    ///   <item>Preserving the relative order of knots</item>

<summary>
/// A <see cref="ResourceManager"/> which serves a .NET Framework assembly's resources on
/// runtimes without BinaryFormatter.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// Grasshopper plugins built from the classic .NET Framework template embed their icons
/// in .resx files as Bitmaps, which the compiler stores as BinaryFormatter blobs. The
/// class generated from each .resx reads them through a stock <see cref="ResourceManager"/>,
/// which needs BinaryFormatter and so fails from .NET 9 on. <see cref="Attach"/> replaces
/// the manager cached in every such generated class - C# Properties.Resources, extra .resx
/// files and VB.NET My.Resources alike - so every lookup goes through
/// <see cref="LegacyResourceSet"/> instead. Ported from Rhino.Inside.Revit
/// (mcneel/rhino.inside-revit@d8e0edc).
/// <para>
/// Grasshopper swallows exceptions thrown by component icon getters, so a failure here
/// shows only as a blank icon. Debug builds therefore throw on failure; release builds log
/// it and leave the assembly as it was.
/// </para>
/// </remarks>
/// <seealso cref="LegacyResourceSet"/>
